interval.visibleText:
CUDA global memory coalescing means combining the addresses requested by active lanes of a warp for one memory instruction into as few memory accesses as possible. Nearby addresses usually coalesce well; widely strided addresses usually require more accesses.

For a concrete example, assume a 32-lane warp, all lanes active, each loading one 4-byte float, and a base address
